newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee holds onto gains in afternoon trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee holds onto gains in afternoon trade.

text.p: London robusta coffee futures remained sharply higher in afternoon trade on strong industry buying, traders said on Tuesday.
Benchmark November ended $24 up at $1,504, below the afternoon session high of $1,520. Volume was 4,732 lots.
"The main thrust of this morning was industry buying coming closer to the market. This afternoon followed very similiar patterns," one trader said.
November ended the morning session $30 higher at $1,510 a tonne in what traders said was an unexpected correction to an oversold situation.
"Everything points to the market being a bit overdone and it is a bit of a correction on that as well," a trader said.
Most of the buying in Europe came ahead of the peak European roasting period, as industry worked to replenish whittled down stock. Most came out of the U.S. but some European buying was also noted.

Traders said they believed the market largely ignored news that the International Coffee Organization (ICO) in a document on Tuesday estimated 1996/97 world coffee production at 99.7 million 60-kg bags against 85.6 million in the 1995/96 period.
"The ICO thing, yes people did look at it, but I don't think it has been a factor in the market today," a trader said.
